title: Endolysosomal Proteomics in Goat Atrial Tissue Using Density-Gradient Approach
author: Ayagama, Berridge, et al.

steps.title: Induce atrial fibrillation in goats
steps.instruction: Induce and maintain AF in N=4 farm‑reared female goats (Capra hircus) for 6 months; include N=4 sham control goats (24–34 months, 72 ± 8 kg). Surgically implant pericardial electrodes above the left atrium under anesthesia with sufentanil and propofol, allow a 2‑week recovery, then induce AF using a subcutaneous neurostimulator and maintain for 3–4 weeks. For terminal open‑chest experiments, anesthetize with sufentanil, propofol and rocuronium.

steps.title: Perfuse heart and collect atrial biopsies
steps.instruction: After euthanasia, perfuse the heart with saline to clear blood, excise left atrial biopsies from a consistent region, wash each biopsy thoroughly with phosphate‑buffered saline (PBS), ensure at least 100 mg tissue per sample, place each biopsy in a freezer‑safe, labeled vial, snap‑freeze in liquid nitrogen within seconds, then store at –80 °C. Collect eight biopsies (one per animal) for the experiment.

steps.title: Reduce and alkylate protein samples
steps.instruction: Add 5 µL of 200 mM dithiothreitol to each sample and incubate 30 min at room temperature (RT); then add 20 µL of 200 mM iodoacetamide and incubate another 30 min at RT.

steps.title: Methanol‑chloroform precipitation of proteins
steps.instruction: Adjust each sample to a total volume of 200 µL (split into multiple tubes if >200 µL; add double‑distilled water if <200 µL). To each tube add 600 µL methanol, 150 µL chloroform, vortex, then add 450 µL Milli‑Q water and vortex 1 min. Centrifuge at 13 000 rpm (maximum speed) at RT for 1 min until the supernatant is clear (extend if turbid). Carefully remove the upper aqueous phase without disturbing the precipitate, add 450 µL methanol, vortex, and centrifuge again at 13 000 rpm, RT, 2 min; discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Resuspend protein pellet in urea buffer
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 6 M urea prepared in 400 mM Tris‑HCl, pH 7.8, then add 250 µL of 400 mM Tris‑HCl to dilute the solution from 6 M to 1 M urea.

steps.title: Digest proteins with trypsin
steps.instruction: Add trypsin at a 1:50 (enzyme:sample) volume ratio, place tubes on a rocker and incubate at 37 °C overnight (≈18 h). After incubation, acidify each sample to a final concentration of 1 % formic acid to stop the digestion.

steps.title: Desalt peptides using Sola‑HRP‑SPE cartridges
steps.instruction: Condition each Sola‑HRP‑SPE cartridge (Thermo Fisher, catalogue no 60109‑001) with 100 % acetonitrile, allowing the solvent to pass by gravity or gentle vacuum. Prepare the sorbent by adding 0.1 % formic acid and let it flow completely. Load each peptide sample slowly onto the cartridge, allowing binding by gravity or gentle vacuum. Wash the cartridge with 0.1 % formic acid to remove salts and hydrophilic impurities. Elute bound peptides with acetonitrile and collect eluate in clean LC‑MS vials or low‑protein‑binding microcentrifuge tubes.

steps.title: Dry peptide eluates in SpeedVac
steps.instruction: Transfer eluates (volume < 1 mL) to low‑binding tubes or LC‑MS vials, place tubes evenly in a SpeedVac rotor with counterbalance tubes containing equal volume of water or buffer, avoid sealing tightly (use vented caps), turn on the vacuum pump and run the drying cycle while monitoring progress through the transparent lid or display.

steps.title: Further desalting and LC‑MS peptide separation
steps.instruction: Perform a second desalting on PepMAP C18 material (300 µm × 5 mm, 5 µm particles) at a flow rate of 20 µL min⁻¹ for 1 min. Separate peptides on an EASY‑Spray column (PepMAP C18, 75 mm × 3500 mm, 2 µm particles, ES803) using a 60‑min gradient from 2 % to 35 % acetonitrile in 5 % DMSO, 0.1 % formic acid, at a flow rate of 250 nL min⁻¹. Run the separation on an Ultimate 3000 UHPLC coupled to an Orbitrap Fusion Lumos mass spectrometer, following the standard parameters described in the LC‑MS workflow document. Complete steps 17–26 consecutively; total minimum time ≈72 h.

steps.title: Process raw MS data with Progenesis QI
steps.instruction: Import raw MS files into Progenesis QI (Waters™ Cooperation, version 4.2). Enable automatic processing and retention‑time alignment, set peak‑picking window between 10 and 75 min, and perform peptide identification and quantification.

steps.title: Statistical analysis in Perseus
steps.instruction: Export protein intensity values to Perseus (v1.6.15.0). Filter out proteins with excessive missing values, retaining 2 104 proteins from TL and EL samples. Log₂‑transform and Z‑score normalize the data without imputation. Perform principal component analysis, generate volcano plots using two‑way Student’s t‑tests, and determine significance with permutation‑based FDR 5 % (250 randomizations, S0 = 0.1). Use the UniProt Capra hircus database (UP000291000) for database searches.

steps.title: Generate protein interaction network with STRING
steps.instruction: Upload the list of significantly regulated proteins to STRING (Version 11). Set interaction evidence to include published databases, experiments, gene fusions, co‑occurrences, and co‑expressions, and select a medium interaction score. Restrict the network to the query proteins only (do not add external interactors). Analyze the network to interpret organelle protein dysregulation in AF.

steps.title: Data analysis timing
steps.instruction: The analysis stage is not time‑dependent and can be performed over 48 h to several days or weeks.
